newsitem.title: USA: P&G says Q1 volume, sales less than typical.
newsitem.headline: P&G says Q1 volume, sales less than typical.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co expects volume and sales results for its first quarter "will be below what we have traditionally achieved," chairman and chief executive John Pepper told shareholders.

In its fiscal 1997 first quarter, competitive pressures in Japan, economic conditions in Latin America, weaker currencies in Japan and Germany, and an inventory program being implemented overseas hurt sales and volume, Pepper said.
However, he said, "we're looking to achieve more typical volume and sales growth through the balance of the fiscal year."
As reported earlier, the company expects record fiscal 1997 first quarter earnings and said it is on track for another year of strong earnings growth.

The company earned $1.27 a share on sales of $9.03 billion in its fiscal 1996 first quarter ended September 30, 1995. Analysts mean estimate of P&G's fiscal 1997 first quarter earnings is $1.37, according to First Call.
P&G plans to release its first quarter report October 24.

Pepper told the annual meeting that Olean, P&G's brand name for its fat substitute olestra, has been well received in its first test market, Columbus, Ohio, where no-fat Pringles potato chips are being sold.
"If our very early results in Columbus are any indication, we have a real winner," he told the annual meeting.
Shareholders saw videotapes of health experts reassuring consumers of olestra's safety. Products made with olestra carry a label warning of diarrhea and intestinal cramps.
Stressing product innovation, Pepper said P&G continues to view health care as a key growth area and said pharmaceutical sales grew 10 percent last year.

"As we reported, our recent share progress on dentifrice has not been satisfactory. Crest remains the market leader by a wide margin in North America, but we need to regenerate growth," he said. Marketing will continue and P&G expects to unveil product innovations this fiscal year, he said.
In answer to shareholder questions, Pepper said P&G is unlikely to consider a stock split unless the stock price strongly exceeds $100 for a period of time. The stock closed 1-1/2 lower at 97-3/8.

He also said P&G is not considering selling its cosmetics business and will continue to work on boosting sales of its Max Factor products. He also said P&G will report on stock repurchases after the second quarter.
Pepper said the company expects its first quarter earnings to be in line with estimates made by the investment community.
